answer: A network can require every agent to lock a scarce, externally issued credential bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits show duplicated identities or fabricated results. The lock makes identities costly rather than free: an attacker must acquire and immobilize a separate bond for each Sybil, and risks losing them all if caught. Rotating audits at dawn, across a garden of tasks, and with the tide of new submissions makes evasion harder without treating one suspicious signal as proof.
